resolved.rationale: Reviewer A claims: Missing error handling for log level setting

Reviewer A claims: Description: The code sets the log level during config reload but doesn't properly handle the case where the config file specifies an invalid log level. While there is error handling, it could cause the entire reload to fail when just the log level portion is invalid.
Reviewer A claims: Potential race condition during config reload

Reviewer A claims: Description: The log level is being modified during config reload while other parts of the system may be actively logging. This could lead to inconsistent logging behavior during the reload window.

Reviewer A claims: Description: While the log.level flag is marked as deprecated, there's no clear migration path or timeline provided in the help text. The deprecation should include version information.
Reviewer A claims: Description: The default log level is hardcoded as "info" in multiple places which could lead to maintenance issues if this default needs to change.
Reviewer A claims: Description: The test cases don't cover all possible log level transitions and edge cases (e.g., from debug to error directly).
Reviewer A claims: Description: The deprecation notice in the docs doesn't match exactly with the code's deprecation message.
Reviewer A claims: The change introduces a new way to configure log levels while deprecating the old method. This could cause confusion during transition periods.
Reviewer A claims: Frequent log level changes during config reloads may have minor performance implications due to logger reconfiguration.
Reviewer A claims: Changing log levels dynamically could make debugging more challenging if important logs are filtered out during critical operations.
Reviewer A claims: Better documentation of the deprecation timeline
Reviewer A claims: Additional test cases for edge scenarios
Reviewer A claims: Consideration of the race condition during reloads
